newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei drop could erase Japan banks' profit-broker.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei drop could erase Japan banks' profit-broker.

text.p: The top 20 Japanese banks could see their unrealised stock profits wiped out if the Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei average falls to around the 15,000 level, Goldman Sachs (Japan) said.

In addition, if the average fell to 13,495, major banks would go into the red this financial year as appraisal losses on their stockholdings would be larger than their operating profits, Goldman said in its market commentary.
The situation would worsen if the Nikkei average fell to 12,137, cutting major banks' core self-asset ratio to below four percent, it said.
The Tokyo stock market's Nikkei index plunged 770 points, or 4.26 percent, to 17,303.65 on Friday.
Stock declines have halved the banks' unrealised stock profits to just below eight trillion yen, compared with levels at the end of September last year, analysts said.

(A) represents the level of the key Nikkei average where each bank's unrealised profits from stockholdings would be erased and (B) is the level where their stock appraisal losses would be larger than operating profits:

The full names of the banks are: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd, Sakura Bank Ltd , Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, Fuji Bank Ltd , Tokai Bank Ltd , Asahi Bank Ltd, Daiwa Bank Ltd, Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp, Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Nippon Trust Bank Ltd, Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
